claim: The Firenze Card costs EUR 85 for a 72-hour pass covering more than 60 museums in the Firenzecard circuit.
quote: a 72 hour pass to access more than 60 museums in the Firenzecard circuit

claim: Firenzecard Restart, a 48-hour extension, becomes available March 1, 2026 priced at EUR 28, having been free until end of 2025.
quote: Firenzecard Restart ... will become available March 1, 2026, priced at EUR 28 ... free until the end of 2025

claim: The Firenze Card is generally not worth it for a weekend; it makes sense only if visiting at least 7-8 major museums, otherwise pre-booked individual tickets cost less.
quote: You're in Florence for at least 3 days! ... no clear cut answer if you're making a decision based solely on the cost of the card

claim: The Duomo complex monuments are no longer part of the Firenze Card circuit and must be bought as separate tickets.
quote: the monuments around the Duomo are no longer part of the FirenzeCard circuit so you need to buy those tickets separately

claim: The Firenze Card is EUR 85 for 72 hours; Duomo sites are excluded but a separate Duomo pass costs about EUR 30, and a new Uffizi+Accademia combo ticket (EUR 26 for 48 hours) launched March 2026 undercuts the card for those only visiting those two.
quote: a new combo ticket (EUR 26 for 48 hours) launched in March 2026 is dramatically cheaper than the Firenze Card ... you can buy a separate Duomo pass for EUR 30

claim: Florence's accommodation tax is tiered by hotel star rating: one-star EUR 4 up to five-star at EUR 10 per adult per night, charged per person per night and capped at ten nights with under-tens exempt.
quote: one-star hotels at EUR 4, four-star at EUR 7.50, and five-star hitting a ceiling of EUR 10 per adult per night ... The charge stops at ten nights ... Under-tens are free

claim: Short-term rentals in Florence are taxed at a flat rate per night and must display a national CIN registration code on the listing.
quote: Short-term rentals are taxed at EUR 5.50 per night and must display a national CIN registration code on their listing

claim: Reservations for the Accademia and Uffizi are highly recommended; reserve the Accademia at least two months and the Uffizi at least one month ahead, as lines form early and peak slots sell out.
quote: Reserve your entry to the Accademia at least two months in advance, if possible; to the Uffizi, at least one month in advance if you want your pick of times

claim: Climbing the Duomo's dome always requires advance reservations, which eliminated the formerly normal long queues.
quote: Climbing the dome of Florence Cathedral always requires advance reservations ... before they were required for climbing the Duomo's dome, long queues were the norm

claim: Shoulder season (March, April, October) is considered the best time to visit Florence, with late September-October offering ideal 60-72F weather, manageable crowds, and 20-30% lower hotel rates than summer.
quote: late September-October combines ideal weather (60-72F), manageable crowds, and 20-30% lower hotel rates than summer

claim: Florence summers are torrid with July-August highs of 38-40C (100-104F), and mid-May through end of July sees peak visitor numbers.
quote: temperatures as high as 38-40C (100-104F) ... Mid May through to the end of July is when visitor numbers are at their highest

claim: Florence's historic centre is closed to traffic except residents, taxis and buses, with Piazza del Duomo, Via Tornabuoni, Piazza della Signoria and Piazza Pitti fully pedestrian-only in the daytime.
quote: fully pedestrian-only areas, with only taxis (and ambulances and a few others) allowed to move around in the daytime

claim: The ZTL Centro Storico is split into camera-enforced sectors (A, B, O, F, G) operating Mon-Fri 07:30-20:00 and Sat 07:30-16:00 with no tourist permit; fines are EUR 83 per camera and Sundays are unrestricted.
quote: Enforcement runs Mon-Fri 07:30-20:00 and Sat 07:30-16:00 (Sep-Jun), and the standard fine is EUR 83 per camera crossed. On Sundays, the ZTL is NOT active
